title: HTTP status codes
text: HTTP status code 404 means the server could not find the requested resource. Status code 301 indicates that a resource has moved permanently to a new URL. A 503 response tells the client that the server is temporarily unavailable, often because it is overloaded or down for maintenance. Codes in the 2xx range signal success, while codes in the 5xx range signal a server error.

title: Git basics
text: Git stores project history as a directed acyclic graph of commits, and each commit is identified by a SHA-1 hash. The command git rebase replays commits from one branch on top of another, which produces a linear history. A merge commit has two parents and records the point where two branches were joined. The staging area, also called the index, holds the changes that will go into the next commit.

title: SQL indexes
text: A B-tree index keeps keys in sorted order, so lookups and range scans take logarithmic time. Adding an index speeds up reads but slows down writes, because every insert or update must also modify the index. A composite index on columns (a, b) can serve queries that filter on a alone, but generally not on b alone. The EXPLAIN statement shows the query plan that the database will use to execute a statement.

title: Docker images and containers
text: A Docker image is built from a Dockerfile, and each instruction creates a new read-only layer. Containers share the host operating system kernel, which makes them lighter than virtual machines. The EXPOSE instruction documents which port a container listens on but does not publish the port. A multi-stage build lets you compile code in one stage and copy only the artifacts into a smaller final image.

title: The Python GIL
text: The Global Interpreter Lock in CPython allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time. Because of the GIL, CPU-bound programs usually use multiprocessing instead of threads to run on several cores. Threads still help with I/O-bound work, since the lock is released while a thread waits on a network or disk operation. Python 3.13 added an experimental free-threaded build that can run without the GIL.

title: BM25 and dense retrieval
text: BM25 is a ranking function that scores documents using term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length. The parameter k1 controls how quickly the score saturates as a term appears more often in a document. The parameter b controls how strongly the score is normalised by document length. Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents as vectors and ranks documents by vector similarity.

title: Transformers
text: The Transformer architecture was introduced in 2017 in the paper Attention Is All You Need. Self-attention lets every token in a sequence weigh the relevance of every other token when building its representation. Positional encodings are added to token embeddings because attention by itself has no notion of word order. Decoder-only models such as GPT generate text one token at a time, conditioning on all the previous tokens.

title: REST API design
text: An HTTP method is idempotent if repeating the same request leaves the server in the same state as sending it once. GET, PUT and DELETE are defined as idempotent methods, while POST is not. A PATCH request applies a partial update to a resource, whereas PUT replaces the whole resource. Pagination with a cursor is more stable than page numbers when rows are inserted while a client is reading.

title: Amazon S3
text: Amazon S3 stores data as objects inside buckets, and every object is addressed by a key. S3 offers eleven nines of durability, designed as 99.999999999 percent, for objects stored in a standard storage class. Versioning keeps every version of an object, which lets you recover from accidental overwrites and deletions. A presigned URL grants temporary access to a private object without sharing credentials.

title: OAuth 2.0
text: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that lets an application obtain limited access to a user account on another service. In the authorization code flow, the client exchanges a short-lived code for an access token at the token endpoint. A refresh token is used to obtain a new access token after the old one expires, without asking the user to log in again. PKCE adds a code challenge to the authorization code flow so that intercepted codes cannot be redeemed by an attacker.

title: Algorithm complexity
text: Merge sort runs in O(n log n) time in the worst case and needs O(n) extra space. Quicksort has an average running time of O(n log n) but degrades to O(n^2) when pivots are chosen badly. A hash table gives average constant-time lookups, but the worst case is linear when many keys collide. Binary search needs a sorted array and takes O(log n) comparisons.

title: Kubernetes objects
text: A Kubernetes pod is the smallest deployable unit and can run one or more containers that share a network namespace. A Deployment manages a ReplicaSet and performs rolling updates of the pods it controls. A Service gives a set of pods a stable IP address and DNS name, even as the individual pods are replaced. The kubelet runs on every node and makes sure the containers described in the pod specifications are running.
